title: Apprenticeship review
intro: My apprenticeship at Lysarc followed one thread: a mission that started in business intelligence and moved towards data engineering and software development. Here is what I take from it, on the technical, professional and personal side.

sections.title: Technical review
body: I covered a broad chain: data modelling and decision-support indicators, data processing in SAS, Python application development (MVC, tests, packaging), and an exploration of a fully local AI architecture. The common thread: real-world data, imperfect and under confidentiality constraints.
My main progression was moving from execution to design: choosing an architecture, justifying it, documenting it, and keeping it alive over time.
What I still want to improve: putting AI tools into production, and industrialising data pipelines.

sections.title: Professional review
body: I was the only Data Analyst in the organisation. That autonomy forced me to formalise my choices for a non-specialist audience, and to make documentation and training part of every deliverable.
I learned to run three projects in parallel on different rhythms, to trade off between new features and stabilising existing ones, and to accept a project being paused when priorities change.
I worked with data managers, SAS programmers, biostatisticians, project managers, a doctor, the CIO and the DPO. Adapting my vocabulary to each person was a constant exercise.

sections.title: Personal review
body: Being the only referent for a role, with no technical safety net, was demanding but formative. I gained confidence in my ability to decide and to own my choices.
Working on data about cancer patients gives concrete meaning to the demands of quality and confidentiality.
My commitments alongside, sailing instructor and scout camp director, feed the same things as my work: leading, passing on, organising.

devenu.title: The professional I've become
devenu.body: I arrived on the internship as a student running analysis tasks. I finish the apprenticeship having designed and defended a method, a data architecture and a small suite of tools, and having supported a team. I now sit between data analysis, data engineering and software development.

projetPostBut.title: After the BUT
projetPostBut.body: Since September 2026 I've been at an engineering school, INSA Lyon, aiming for Data Engineer and AI Engineer roles. Industrialising data processing, system administration, and the local architecture I keep experimenting with on my homelab are exactly what I want to go deeper on.
